title: Many connections, one loop
description:
Model a server that handles many clients in one loop, the way `select` or `poll` servers do.

```
client 1 sent "NAME ada\n"   -> "hello ada"
client 2 sent "NAME b"       -> (waiting for the rest of the line)
client 2 sent "ob\nTIME\n"   -> "hello bob", "time is 12:00"
client 1 closed              -> 1 client left
```
hints: `while ((pos = buffer.find('\n')) != std::string::npos)` takes out one line at a time (lesson 2.04).
The real version calls `poll` with every socket and calls `onData` for each one that is readable; the logic here does not change.
requirements: `class Server` keeps one input buffer per client id in a `std::map`.
`onData(id, text)` handles every complete line and keeps partial ones.
`onClose(id)` removes the client. Commands: `NAME x`, `TIME`, `WHO` (lists names).
stretch: Write the real loop with `poll` (Linux) or `WSAPoll` (Windows) on your own machine.
